financials_interim.notes:
Amana Bank PLC, a Shariah-compliant (Islamic) licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). Explicitly a 'stand-alone institution' with 'no subsidiaries, associates, or affiliated institutions' (per its own press release, p.2) apart from a sponsorship relationship with OrphanCare -- so this filing has only a single set of financial statements (no Group/Company split anywhere in the document); entered as a single basis='GROUP' row per this project's convention for single-entity bank filings. This is the FIRST financial_statements/interim_updates entry for ABL in this database. Uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1, six months ended 30 June 2026) columns; the filing also separately provides quarter-only (Apr-Jun) columns on the income statement, not used here except for narrative colour. 

ISLAMIC-FINANCE TERMINOLOGY MAPPING (Amana Bank does not use conventional interest-based wording; each of its captions was mapped to the equivalent conventional-bank concept used by this database's schema): 'Financing Income' (Rs.9,007,346k H1 2026 / Rs.7,990,586k H1 2025 -- income from the Bank's Shariah-compliant financing products: Overdraft, Trade Finance, Lease (Ijara) Receivables, Staff Facilities, Term Financing (Murabaha/Diminishing Musharaka/Wakala-based), and Gold Facilities, per Note 02) was treated as the equivalent of conventional 'interest income'. 'Financing Expenses' (Rs.4,563,464k / Rs.4,157,807k -- the Mudaraba/Wakala depositors' share of profit paid or payable on 'Due to Depositors', the Bank's savings/investment account base) was treated as the equivalent of conventional 'interest expense'. 'Net Financing Income' (Rs.4,443,882k / Rs.3,832,779k) was treated as the equivalent of conventional 'Net Interest Income'. Per bank convention used consistently this session, finance_costs/finance_income are left BLANK -- Financing Expenses (the depositors' profit-share equivalent of interest expense) is already netted into Net Financing Income, matching how conventional banks' interest expense is handled in this schema. 'Financing and Receivables to Other Customers' (Note 02, Rs.157,005,683k net) is the Islamic-finance equivalent of conventional loans and advances (the underlying products are Murabaha/Ijara/Diminishing Musharaka/Wakala-structured, not interest-based loans, but the balance-sheet function -- the Bank's core financing/lending book -- is identical). 'Due to Depositors' (Rs.180,393,264k, split into Mudaraba/Wakala-based Demand, Savings and Time deposit-equivalent products per Note 05) is the equivalent of conventional customer deposits and, consistent with how every other bank entered this session excludes 'Due to Depositors' from borrowings, is EXCLUDED from both short_term_borrowings and long_term_borrowings here (it is deposit/investment account funding, not debt). 

FIELD MAPPING: revenue = 'Total Operating Income' (Rs.5,528,905k / Rs.4,671,491k, p.4) = Net Financing Income + Net Fee & Commission Income + Net Trading Income + Net Gains/(Losses) on FVTPL Financial Investments + Net Gains/(Losses) on Derecognition of Financial Assets + Net Other Operating Income. operating_profit = the Bank's own subtotal 'Operating Profit Before VAT on Financial Services and Social Security Contribution Levy' (Rs.2,498,538k / Rs.2,110,500k), directly analogous to how other banks' pre-VAT/SSCL subtotal was used this session. profit_before_tax = the Bank's own 'Profit Before Tax' line (Rs.1,874,183k / Rs.1,537,984k), AFTER VAT on Financial Services (Rs.548,686k) and Social Security Contribution Levy (Rs.75,669k) -- these two levies (Rs.624,355k combined for H1 2026) are not stored as a separate field, consistent with the convention used for HNB/SAMP/CBNK/NTB/COMB/PABC/DFCC. tax_expense = Rs.749,561k (a genuine, unremarkable increase from Rs.636,650k, no unusual swing or credit -- checked specifically per the narrative-quality instruction; PBT-tax_expense=1,124,622k exactly matches disclosed 'Profit for the Period', so no distortion in the tax line this period). current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention -- this is a liquidity-ordered balance sheet with no trade working-capital concept. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to Banks' (Rs.2,064,956k), the Islamic-finance equivalent of conventional interbank borrowing (Wakala/Mudaraba-based interbank placements accepted from other banks, per the fair-value note's own carrying-value table on p.11-12, which shows this line moving in step with market rates like conventional interbank funding). long_term_borrowings left BLANK: ABL's balance sheet (p.6) has no Sukuk, subordinated Mudaraba/Musharaka capital instrument, or other longer-tenor wholesale funding line -- the only funding-liability captions are 'Due to Banks' (mapped above) and 'Due to Depositors' (excluded as deposit funding); no clean long-term-borrowings analog exists in this filing, so leaving it blank was judged more accurate than forcing a mapping. cash_and_equivalents = Rs.28,072,586k, the Statement of Financial Position's own 'Cash and Cash Equivalents' line (net of Rs.5,607k allowance for impairment per the cash-flow note on p.7). capex = Rs.2,993,752k, 'Acquisition of Property, Plant & Equipment' from the cash flow statement (p.8) -- this quarter's capex is unusually large because it includes the Bank's new corporate office premises acquired in Q2 2026 for ~Rs.2.7bn (per the press release, p.2, and explanatory Note 8, p.15); Acquisition of Intangible Assets (Rs.246,005k) was kept separate and not folded into capex, consistent with standard PPE-only capex definition. shares_in_issue = 551,222,806 (Note 09, Twenty Largest Shareholders schedule, p.16, 'Total' row), cross-checked two ways: (1) against EPS -- Rs.1,124,622k PAT / 551,222,806 shares = Rs.2.0403, matching the disclosed Basic/Diluted EPS of Rs.2.04 exactly; (2) against Net Asset Value per share -- Rs.26,072,372k total equity / 551,222,806 shares = Rs.47.30, matching the disclosed NAV/share of Rs.47.30 exactly. Both cross-checks confirm the share count. Accounting identities tie out exactly: Total Assets (Rs.215,230,243k) = Total Liabilities (Rs.189,157,871k) + Total Equity (Rs.26,072,372k); Profit Before Tax (Rs.1,874,183k) - Tax Expense (Rs.749,561k) = Profit for the Period (Rs.1,124,622k). Page citations: Statement of Profit or Loss p.4, Statement of Financial Position p.6, Statement of Cash Flows p.8 (all '=== PAGE N ===' markers in the extraction correspond to physical PDF pages).

interim_updates.note_text: Amana Bank (ABL), a Shariah-compliant bank marking its 15th Anniversary in H1 2026, delivered its best-ever half-year performance: Profit After Tax grew 24.8% YoY to Rs.1,124,622k, surpassing Rs.1bn for the first time, while Profit Before Tax grew 21.9% to Rs.1,874,183k. Growth accelerated into Q2: quarterly PBT rose 29.3% YoY to Rs.1,032,548k and quarterly PAT rose 33.3% to Rs.622,661k. Net Financing Income (the Islamic-finance equivalent of Net Interest Income -- income from Murabaha/Ijara/Diminishing Musharaka/Term Financing products less the Mudaraba depositors' share of profit) grew 15.9% YoY to Rs.4,443,882k, supported by a steady Financing Margin (the Bank's own equivalent of Net Interest Margin) of 4.3%, unchanged from year-end 2025. Net Fee and Commission Income grew 16.1% to Rs.711,350k. Total Operating Income rose 18.4% to Rs.5,528,905k, aided by Net Trading Income more than doubling (+60.5% to Rs.354,777k, mainly FX-related). Impairment charges grew a moderate 11.1% YoY to Rs.159,575k, in line with growth in the financing book rather than a deterioration in credit quality -- indeed the Net Impaired Financing (Stage 3) Ratio improved to 1.1% from 1.2% at year-end 2025, and the Gross ratio held flat at 2.8%. Total Operating Expenses grew 18.8% to Rs.2,870,792k, driven by Depreciation and Amortisation +34.4% (Rs.177,742k to Rs.238,931k, reflecting the new corporate office and IT investment) and Other Operating Expenses +26.0% (Rs.979,296k to Rs.1,233,917k); Personnel Expenses grew a more modest 11.9% to Rs.1,397,944k. Despite this cost growth, the Bank's own Cost-to-Income Ratio improved to 51.2% from 51.8% at year-end 2025 (and to 51% for H1 from 52% at end-Q1), as revenue growth outpaced costs. The tax line grew in line with pre-tax profit (Tax Expense +17.7% to Rs.749,561k against PBT +21.9%) with no unusual swing, credit, or one-off item -- the Bank's aggregate tax contribution (VAT on Financial Services + SSCL + income tax, Rs.1,373,916k) represented a very high 55% of Operating Profit before all taxes, a structural feature of Sri Lanka's bank taxation rather than a period-specific distortion. Total Assets grew 5.3% since December 2025 to Rs.215,230,243k, boosted in Q2 by the acquisition of the Bank's new corporate office premises for ~Rs.2.7bn (PP&E and ROU assets rose from Rs.3,278,103k to Rs.6,075,965k, +85.4%); the Bank's Board has approved disposing of its former office at 486 Galle Road, Colombo 3. Customer financing receivables grew 4.0% to Rs.157,005,683k (net), driven by SME financing growth, while Due to Depositors (the deposit-equivalent) grew 4.8% to Rs.180,393,264k, with an industry-leading CASA ratio of 45.2%. Return on Equity improved to 8.9% (from 8.1% in Q1 2026 and 7.8% in H1 2025) and Return on Assets stood at 1.8%. Capital and liquidity remained comfortably above regulatory minimums despite the property acquisition: Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio 12.4% (vs 7.0% minimum, though down from 13.0% at year-end 2025), Total Capital Ratio 13.8% (vs 12.5% minimum), Rupee Liquidity Coverage Ratio 321.8% and Net Stable Funding Ratio 144.2% (both vs 100% minimum).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is the FIRST financial_statements/interim_updates entry for ABL in this database (no prior row of any period existed before this one). Reporting basis: ABL is a single-entity filer (no subsidiaries) and reports only cumulative six-month figures alongside separate quarter-only (Apr-Jun) columns on the income statement; this entry stores the H1 CUMULATIVE (six months ended 30 June 2026) figures, consistent with how other banks were entered this session, with quarter-only figures used only for narrative colour (e.g. Q2 PAT +33.3% YoY) above.
interim_updates.takeaway: This is a genuinely clean beat, not a one-off: PAT growth (+24.8% YoY, accelerating to +33.3% in Q2 alone) is broad-based across Net Financing Income (+15.9%), fee income (+16.1%) and trading income (+60.5%), with impairment charges rising only in line with book growth and asset quality actually improving (Net Stage 3 ratio down to 1.1% from 1.2%); the tax line moved proportionately with pre-tax profit with no credit or swing to explain away. The main watch item is cost growth (Total Operating Expenses +18.8%, driven by depreciation on the new ~Rs.2.7bn corporate office and higher other operating costs) running close to revenue growth, though the Bank's own Cost-to-Income Ratio still improved modestly to 51.2%. Capital ratios (CET1 12.4%, down from 13.0% at year-end 2025) softened somewhat after the office acquisition but remain well above regulatory minimums.

operational_highlights: PAT +24.8% YoY to Rs.1,124,622k (H1 2026), the Bank's best-ever half-year and first time surpassing Rs.1bn; PBT +21.9% to Rs.1,874,183k; Q2 alone PAT +33.3% YoY to Rs.622,661k, PBT +29.3% to Rs.1,032,548k

Net Financing Income (Islamic-finance equivalent of Net Interest Income) +15.9% YoY to Rs.4,443,882k on a steady 4.3% Financing Margin; Net Fee and Commission Income +16.1% to Rs.711,350k; Net Trading Income more than doubled, +60.5% to Rs.354,777k

Impairment charges +11.1% YoY to Rs.159,575k, growing broadly in line with the financing book rather than signalling credit deterioration -- Net Impaired Financing (Stage 3) Ratio improved to 1.1% from 1.2% at year-end 2025

Total Operating Expenses +18.8% to Rs.2,870,792k, led by Depreciation & Amortisation +34.4% (new corporate office/IT investment) and Other Operating Expenses +26.0%; Cost-to-Income Ratio nonetheless improved to 51.2% from 51.8% at year-end 2025

Total Assets +5.3% since December 2025 to Rs.215,230,243k, driven partly by the Bank's acquisition of new corporate office premises for ~Rs.2.7bn in Q2 2026 (PP&E and ROU assets +85.4% to Rs.6,075,965k); Board has approved disposal of the former Galle Road office

Customer financing receivables +4.0% to Rs.157,005,683k (net), driven by SME growth; Due to Depositors +4.8% to Rs.180,393,264k with a 45.2% CASA ratio; ROE improved to 8.9% (from 7.8% H1 2025); CET1 Ratio 12.4% (down from 13.0% at year-end 2025) and Total Capital Ratio 13.8%, both comfortably above regulatory minimums
key_drivers: Broad-based Total Operating Income growth (+18.4% to Rs.5,528,905k) across Net Financing Income (+15.9%), Net Fee & Commission Income (+16.1%) and Net Trading Income (+60.5%) is the primary driver of PBT/PAT growth -- not a single distorting item

Impairment charge growth (+11.1%) trails financing-book growth and coincides with an IMPROVING Net Stage 3 ratio (1.1% vs 1.2%), indicating the impairment increase reflects book growth/prudent provisioning rather than deteriorating asset quality

Depreciation & Amortisation (+34.4% YoY) and Other Operating Expenses (+26.0%) are the main cost drivers, largely tied to the Bank's acquisition of new corporate office premises (~Rs.2.7bn) in Q2 2026, a one-time capital investment rather than a recurring cost base shift

The tax expense line (+17.7% YoY) moved proportionately with PBT (+21.9%) with no credit, reversal, or unusual swing -- the aggregate 55% effective tax/levy burden on Operating Profit before all taxes (VAT on Financial Services + SSCL + income tax) is a structural feature of Sri Lankan bank taxation, not a period-specific distortion to PAT growth
